sub_indicators.label: Fibre routes to the rest of the world
sub_indicators.subject: infra.connect
sub_indicators.text: International internet bandwidth: fibre routes to the rest of the world
sub_indicators.norm_short: The African Union's Digital Transformation Strategy asks every member state for at least two international connections, and for operators to share infrastructure.
criteria: A source from the past three years says the country has no international fibre route: satellite or microwave only.
One fibre route carries the country's internet traffic abroad: a submarine cable landing in the country, or a fibre link through a neighbour.
Two or more international fibre routes are in service, though they share one landing station or one neighbour.
Two of the routes share no landing station: cables at different stations, a cable and a land link, or for a country without a coast, links through two neighbours.
Two independent routes, and other operators buy capacity at the landing station or on the cable, or it runs on open-access or regulated wholesale terms.

aspects.name: One route, two, and two independent
